description:
ZKTeco/eSSL ADMS push receiver (plain Django view, CSRF-exempt, outside DRF). Gated by flag `ADMS_RECEIVER` (404 JSON `not_found` while off). Authentication is the secret token in the path **and** the `SN` the request states: they must belong to the same device, which must be active, `adms_enabled` and (if it has an allow-list) pushing from an allowed IP. Every reply is HTTP 200 `text/plain; charset=utf-8` with explicit Content-Length. Every request is recorded as evidence (`devices_adms_request`, token redacted). No SN → `OK`, evidence only; unknown token or SN not matching the token → `OK`, serial quarantined (UNKNOWN_SERIAL/TOKEN_MISMATCH), nothing ingested; refused device → `OK`, evidence only. Throttled per token (`iclock` 300/min): beyond it the reply is `ERROR` and nothing is recorded. A failure inside the server answers `ERROR` so the terminal resends.

**Catch-all** `^(?P<endpoint>.*)$`: any other path under `/iclock/<token>/` (e.g. `querydata`, `rtdata`, `fdata`, or a nested path) reaches the same receiver. The endpoint name is classified by substring (`cdata`, `getrequest`, `devicecmd`, `registry`, `ping` anywhere in it behave like the named endpoint); anything else is recorded as kind UNKNOWN and answered `OK` — never rejected, so unfamiliar firmware does not retry forever. An admitted UNKNOWN request still counts as contact from the terminal. Methods outside GET/POST/PUT/DELETE get `OK` unrecorded.
